name: Eating for jaw (chewing hard foods)
lead: Eating for jaw is the practice of regularly chewing tough or hard foods in the hope of enlarging the masseter and sharpening the jawline. It is discussed in looksmaxxing communities alongside mastic gum and jaw exercisers.

The masseter is one of the muscles of mastication and can enlarge in people who habitually clench or grind their teeth or chew gum, typically painlessly and sometimes asymmetrically.[1] No studies were found testing hard-food diets for facial appearance.

paras: The masseter elevates the jaw and is among the strongest chewing muscles. Reference material reports that habitual clenching, bruxism and constant gum chewing can enlarge it, sometimes causing facial asymmetry and temporomandibular joint problems.[1]

card.summary: Chewing tough foods to grow the masseter; the muscle can enlarge with heavy chewing, but hard-food diets are untested.
card.note: Overuse of the jaw is associated with TMJ problems in reference material.

quick.overview:
Eating for jaw means chewing hard, chewy foods to build the masseter and define the jawline.

The masseter can enlarge with habitual clenching or gum chewing, but no studies test hard-food diets for looks.
quick.mechanism: Repeated loading of the jaw-closing muscles may enlarge them, as seen with bruxism and constant gum chewing.
quick.risks: Reference material links masseter enlargement to facial asymmetry and temporomandibular joint problems.
